results.summary_before: This design is a driver for a hexagonal charlieplexed LED matrix with columns of 3-4-5-4-3 pixels. It accepts serial data on ui[0] while ui[1] is low, loading the pattern column-wise, and then drives the matrix through five bidirectional pins when ui[1] is high. Testing requires an external charlieplexed LED display (or individual LEDs) connected to the uio pins, with the clock pulsed at 100 Hz or more. The project is notable for targeting a non-rectangular charlieplexed matrix and is implemented in Wokwi.

results.summary_before: This design tests servo signals by lighting up eight LEDs according to the pulse width of the input signal. A 1 ms pulse (0 degrees) lights no LEDs, while a 2 ms pulse (180 degrees) lights all eight. It requires an external 4 kHz clock, eight LEDs with resistors, and a servo signal on input 0. The design uses flip-flops to process the servo signal and is implemented in Wokwi.

results.summary_before: This design is a hardware implementation of the Bivium-B stream cipher used as a non-linear feedback shift register (NLFSR). It includes a 177-bit NLFSR with feedback taps and an output function, and it provides eight outputs that expose internal register values for self-testing. The circuit can be initialized to all zeros and then run, with outputs compared against a Python simulation. External hardware such as a logic analyzer is needed to observe the outputs, and the design is notable for its use of a stream cipher as a PRNG.

results.summary_before: This chip decodes the QOA audio format, a simple lossy compression for 16-bit PCM audio, via an SPI slave interface. It acts as a co-processor, requiring an external microcontroller to handle file I/O and streaming. The design has been tested in silicon and works, achieving up to 176,056 samples per second. Notable for its compact implementation and potential for real-time audio streaming.
